newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet's sale date up to parliament - minister.
newsitem.headline: Stet's sale date up to parliament - minister.

text.p: Italy's government has done all it can to get the privatisation of state telecoms group Stet underway according to a set timetable and it it is now in the hands of parliament, Post Minister Antonio Maccanico said.
Stet's sale is slated for February/March 1997.
Maccanico was asked by reporters while attending a meeting of financial analysts if a telecoms sector watchdog authority would be legally set up in time to respect the calendar.
Such an authority is essential before the Stet sale takes place.

"The government has done its duty and presented the measures on the authority to parliament on July 17. Now it is all up to the two houses of parliament," he said. The measure is currently going through the upper Senate.
Stet managing director Ernesto Pascale warned on Friday that the privatisation would be delayed unless parliament rapidly approved the bill setting up the sector authority.
He said that if the watchdog had not been approved by the end of November there would not be time to float Stet in February or March.
